question: A streaming service historically converts 30% of free-trial users into paid subscribers. After a redesign, 87 of 240 randomly selected free-trial users became paid subscribers. At the 2.5% significance level, test whether the redesign increased the population conversion rate above 30%. Show the hypotheses, verify that the large-sample proportion test is appropriate, calculate the test statistic and p-value, and state the conclusion in context.

precedents: Maximum leniency: on judgment calls take the higher plausible mark.
No double penalty for propagated errors; one botched chain is one calculation mistake.
A decision that follows correctly from the student's own wrong statistic is not an extra error.
A p-value range containing the method's exact p earns full credit; a range within 0.001 with the decision unchanged reconciles up to full.
Validity computed with observed counts (87, 153) earns full credit.
Wald z (p-hat in the SE) is a calculation variant, no deduction.
Two-sided p quoted but decision still reject: no deduction. Two-sided p with fail to reject: conceptual error.
Conclusion without context loses 0.25 of the conclusion column only when the decision itself is right.
